issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers class defines a method named appendElement (appendElement(T[] array, T element)), but Stock.java in the template calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This name/signature mismatch causes a compilation error and prevents students from building or running the starter project. The solution repository uses addElementToArray, so the template ArrayHelpers method name does not match the rest of the codebase.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers from appendElement to addElementToArray (with the same parameters and return type), or update Stock.java to call appendElement. Preferably standardize on addElementToArray (as used in the solution) so all references compile consistently.

issues.description: The helper method for appending an element to an array is named inconsistently across artifacts. In the template, ArrayHelpers defines the method as appendElement (ArrayHelpers.appendElement) but Stock.java in the template calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray, which does not exist in the template. The solution repository consistently uses addElementToArray. This mismatch (appendElement vs addElementToArray) creates a direct mapping and compilation confusion for students: they see code calling addElementToArray but the provided helper has a different name. Students will waste time reconciling or fixing the naming instead of focusing on the exercise logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across repositories. Rename the template method appendElement to addElementToArray (and keep its signature) so that Stock.addToStockIngredients and other calls compile and match the solution. Alternatively, change calls to ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray to ArrayHelpers.appendElement, but prefer renaming the template helper to addElementToArray to match the solution and any expected usages mentioned in code/comments.
